Step 5 — HBM placement is excluded, and the 3bda thread-complete trace reframes the suspect: a window-wide transient, not one slow component

Two results landed in this step.
  • Card HBM weight placement is EXCLUDED (Bill’s criterion). All 12 draws of the v9 campaign produced the byte-identical HBM allocation sequence (hash 5d680946f58963d4: 868 allocations, 77,035,520 bytes, devices 0–3) while decode TPS still rolled 165.3–172.3. Same addresses, different speed → placement cannot be the cause.
  • The parallel perfetto session on delphi-3bda finished (20/20 draws) and delivered the thread-complete view of the inter-fwd-pass window. It confirms the window carries 96.7% of the per-launch loss (corr −0.956), and adds the key new fact: inside a stalled window, host-only compute also runs 3–5× slower — not just the waits. The stall is a window-wide state that stretches the card stream, the driver waits, and pure host work together.
Where the elimination ladder ended (final state, 2026-08-13): the entire CPU-speed family is excluded with mechanical proof (H1 SMI, H2 C-states, H4 frequency — sections 3–4), the host memory path is excluded as cause AND amplifier (H8 dose-response, both tp2 and tp4 unmoved under an 80 GB/s antagonist), consume chunking and every launch-drawn host variable (placement, seat, dispatch phase) are excluded, and cross-card dispatch reaches all four cards synchronized to ≤10µs in every window. What varies per launch is the per-block delivery cadence of the lm-head stream: the 118-block train trickles uniformly slower in slow draws (median inter-block gap 2.9→3.7µs, +28%; consume work only 62–75µs/fill) — card compute/stream-out pacing, far below link capacity. Remaining avenues: fence-bracketed measurement (tags 7600/7601, in progress), FPGA-team telemetry against the cadence signature, and owner-gated PCIe A/Bs. Details in the addendum (section 5).

1 · v9 result: same HBM addresses every launch, different speed every launch

Method. The v9 probe build (install-kvprobe9, runtron sha 687a0a06f3d22e02…) records every card memory allocation made by alloc_kv_weights and alloc_hardware_weights (src/pos/driver.cpp) into the probe file: device index, address, size, in allocation order. hbm_audit.py hashes the ordered (device, address, size) sequence. If weight placement varied per launch, the hash would vary.

2 · Cross-host: what the 3bda perfetto session saw inside the window

The runbook session ran 20 draws on delphi-3bda with perfetto events gated to open only during the inter-fwd-pass window (last layer, decoding, post-attention), so the forward pass ran unperturbed. All 21 runs kept the reference token hash; TPS stayed in the bare band (170.5–185.3, CV 2.60%) — the lottery rolled normally under tracing. The new fact: pure host work slows down inside stalled windows

  • compute_forward_args (host-only computation, touches no card) runs ×3.3–4.7 slower inside stalled windows; construct_minibatches up to ×12.
  • The card side stretches in the same windows: window start → last lm-head chunk “data ready” grows 247→396µs (corr −0.77), with ~200µs pauses between chunk completions.
  • The fixed-cost part does not move: waiting_for_logits stays ~185→194µs (corr −0.27).
  • All-idle time concentrates at two seams: after the listener callback ends, and between attention-plan assembly and the next step’s first hardware dispatch.
  • Package core frequency looked flat across draws (turbostat 3751–3778 MHz) — but at 5-second cadence, which cannot see a transient lasting hundreds of microseconds. This is a measurement gap, not an exoneration.

2.5 · What exactly is a “stalled window”?

The window (“inter-fwd-pass window” everywhere in this series) is the once-per-token span between two forward passes: it opens when layer 35’s attention barrier releases, covers the lm-head matmul dispatch, the arrival of the 118 streamed logits blocks, fill_logits_buffer, the token-pick callback, and closes when the next step’s first layer-0 work starts. In the perfetto captures it is literally the dense cluster of events between two silent stretches; the extraction tool starts a new window wherever the gated event stream goes silent for more than 1.5 ms (GAP_NS = 1_500_000 in window_gaps.py:18) — the forward pass provides that silence, since the gate keeps perfetto quiet outside the window. A window’s span is then last-span-end minus first-span-start within the cluster (code in the appendix). Note: this 1.5 ms silence splitter and the 1500 µs stall threshold below are the same number by coincidence — one cuts between windows, the other classifies a window’s own length.

A stalled window is a window whose total span exceeds 1500 µs — about 2.5× the quick mode. The threshold is not arbitrary: window durations are not one blob with a shifting mean, they form two populations, and 1500 µs falls in the valley between them:

Sketch of the shape; the per-draw table in the pfgate report carries the measured medians (560–1188 µs) and p90s. The two-population split and the 1500 µs valley are the pfgate report’s finding 2.

Three facts make “stalled window” the right unit of analysis:

  • The lottery is the stall rate. Fast launches: ~6–9% of windows stall. Slow launches: up to 34.6%. The per-draw stall rate tracks decode TPS almost perfectly (window mean vs TPS corr −0.956).
  • Stalled windows look the same everywhere. A stalled window in the fastest draw has the same internal structure and duration distribution as one in the slowest draw. Launches do not draw “how bad”, only “how often”.
  • Stalls arrive memorylessly (section 3, H3): each window is an independent coin flip whose bias is set at launch.

2.6 · How the focus moved from fill_logits_buffer to stalled windows

Through step 3, fill_logits_buffer was the drill-down target because attribution kept pointing at it: largest child of the inter-fwd-pass path, best correlation with TPS. Steps 4 and the pfgate capture changed its role — from suspect to symptom:

In one sentence: fill_logits_buffer did not stop being important — it stopped being a suspect. It is the longest wait inside the window, so a window-wide stall shows up there first and biggest (+181 µs of the +402 µs window growth). But the same stall also slows host-only code (compute_forward_args, no logits involved) and pauses the card’s own chunk completions, so the cause has to sit below all of them — which is why the H-series on this page tests machine-level mechanisms (SMI, C-states, frequency, power, memory path) instead of splitting fill further.

3 · What this changes in the suspect statement

Through step 4 the last suspect standing was “card-internal dynamic state” — because everything measured on the host side looked like waiting. The thread-complete view breaks that framing: in a stalled window the host is not only waiting longer, its own compute is slower, at the same moments the card’s stream chunks pause. One shared condition touches both sides for ~0.5–1.5 ms, more often in slow launches. Hypotheses, each with its test:

hypothesismechanismtest (one causal bit each)status
H1 · SMI (System Management Interrupt) stormsFirmware pauses all CPU cores at once; invisible to the OS scheduler and to 5-second turbostat averages; rate can differ per boot/launch epoch. Read MSR 0x34 (SMI count) before and after each draw’s benchmark; correlate the per-draw delta with TPS. EXCLUDED 16/16 draws: SMI delta = 0 on cpu0 and cpu24 in every draw, while TPS rolled 164.542–170.709 (gap 3.75%, CV 1.13% — the lottery was present). Zero firmware interrupts, fluctuation anyway. Campaign 3c51-smicount-tp4-20260812T164106Z.
H2 · CPU idle-state wake latencyDuring the near-idle start of the window, cores enter deep C-states (hardware sleep levels); waking costs tens of µs per core and cold caches after; per-launch thread placement could set how often this bites. Hold /dev/cpu_dma_latency at 0 for the whole campaign (forces shallow idle states, no reboot, fully reversible). If the lottery collapses (CV ≈ the tight tp1/tp2 level), mechanism found. EXCLUDED campaign 3c51-dmalat0-tp4-20260812T170220Z, 12/12 ok. The suppression provably worked: cpu24 entered the POLL idle state 9.2M more times while the C1/C1E/C6/C6P entry counters did not move at all during the campaign. The lottery did NOT collapse: TPS 148.8–168.8 (CV 2.95%, gap 13.5%; even excluding the two lowest draws, CV 1.43% / gap 5.4% vs baseline 1.13% / 3.75%). Zero deep-sleep wake events, fluctuation anyway. Side finding: the mean dropped ~4% — ~250 idle CPUs spinning in POLL burned package power and slowed the busy cores, so this workload runs against the package power budget.
H3 · stall arrival processWhether stalled windows arrive periodically (external poller), in bursts, or memorylessly separates an interfering activity from a per-launch resource condition. Inter-arrival statistics on the pfgate per-window durations (data already on disk: analysis/out/draw_*/draw_*.gaps.csv). No machine time needed. DONE result below: memoryless.
H4 · core frequency ramp (P-state)Even with the performance governor, the hardware (HWP) may drop core clocks during the near-idle part of the window (floor was 800 MHz vs 4400 MHz max) and re-ramp slowly on wake — slowing host work and stream consumption together. Distinct from H2: this is clock speed, not sleep states. Pin scaling_min_freq = scaling_max_freq (4400 MHz) on all CPUs for a campaign; C-states stay enabled, so there is no power confound like the H2 test. Package energy (RAPL) captured per draw as a cross-check. EXCLUDED campaign 3c51-minfreq-tp4-20260812T172103Z, 12/12 ok, pin verified (min=max=4400000 on all sampled cores, floors restored after). Lottery persisted: TPS 158.019–168.176, CV 1.90%, gap 6.43% (baseline 1.13% / 3.75%). RAPL cross-check: package-0 power was nearly constant across draws (355.0±0.9 W) and correlates positively with TPS (corr +0.80) — power tracks useful work done, the opposite sign of power-limit throttling causing the slowness.
H5 · logits stream-consume path shapeThe lm-head result streams to the host in 118 blocks; host pool workers consume them in chunks (default chunk = worker count). If the consume/DMA interplay on the memory path is the mechanism, changing its shape should change the stall texture or the lottery itself. A/B: TRON_MAX_LOGITS_CHUNK_SIZE=1 (maximally serialized consume) vs today’s baseline; watch CV, stall rate, and the token hash (must stay 66af1d58…). EXCLUDED campaign 3c51-chunk1-tp4-20260812T174040Z, 12/12 ok, arm verified in the recorded environment (TRON_MAX_LOGITS_CHUNK_SIZE=1), token hash unchanged. Lottery persisted: TPS 161.49–169.92, CV 1.72%, gap 5.22% — consume-chunk shape is not the mechanism.
H6 · hardware clipping below the pinned floor (thermal / PL1 / PL2 / EDP)H4 pinned the requested frequency; hardware can still clip below the request on thermal or power-limit events lasting microseconds — invisible to every average captured so far. Package temperature measured at 89 °C under load (TjMax 107). Two MSR tiers per draw (Ben’s suggestion): (1) sticky throttle-reason log bits (0x1B1 / 0x19C / 0x64F) cleared before and read after each benchmark — latch even µs-long events, per cause; (2) a 150µs sampler (msrsamp.c) recording effective frequency (APERF/MPERF), C0 residency, temperatures and package power, TSC-stamped to join individual stalled windows from the kvwait probe. TESTED — CLOCK IS FLAT campaign 3c51-msrsamp-tp4-20260812T175744Z, 12/12 ok. At 150µs resolution, effective frequency inside stalled windows equals quick windows and pre-window control: 2.68–2.71 GHz everywhere, all 12 draws (26–43 stalled windows each); C0 residency ≈1.0; temperatures flat (core 78°C, package 89°C); no thermal/PROCHOT log bits latched in any draw (0x64F reads 0 always on this Xeon — unimplemented, treated as no-data). Consequence: the host-work slowdown inside stalled windows happens at constant clock — same instructions taking more cycles means the cores stall on the memory path (cache/DRAM/UPI), which is also what pauses the card’s stream chunks. Side finding: this host’s tron cores run at 2.70 GHz effective (base clock) with the power-limitation status bit steadily asserted — a steady-state condition, not a per-launch differentiator, and it explains why the H4 floor pin changed nothing here.
H7 · memory-path interference (DMA burst vs host work)The lm-head stream DMA and host work share the memory subsystem (and DDIO shares the L3 cache). If slow launches draw an unlucky memory-path condition, stalls hit both sides at once — matching every observation so far. Per-draw uncore counters over the benchmark: IMC CAS read/write per socket, LLC loads and misses. Compare slow vs fast draws: more bytes moved, or a worse miss rate, or a socket imbalance → memory-path lottery confirmed. AGGREGATES FLAT campaign 3c51-uncore-tp4-20260812T182045Z, 12/12 ok. Socket-0 reads 583–586 GiB in every draw (fixed work: 4096 tokens), LLC miss rate 22.8–23.2%, socket 1 near idle, all correlations weak (|corr| ≤ 0.42). No bulk per-launch memory-path difference — whatever differs lives only inside the windows (~1.5% of wall time), invisible to whole-draw counters. Structural fact: software attention streams the K/V cache from host DRAM at ~19.5 GB/s sustained — this workload leans on the host memory path by design.
Seat theory (analysis-only, pfgate data)If a different pool worker won the logits-consume job each launch, the seat’s cache/neighbor geometry could be the per-launch draw. Which thread ran fill_logits_buffer in each of ~3800 windows × 20 draws (seat_analysis.py). DEAD One thread per launch runs ALL fills — and it is the SAME seat every launch (worker 0 on cpu 25, 20/20 draws). The seat cannot be the lottery variable.
Cross-card stream phase (analysis-only, pfgate data)The 4 cards’ DMA bursts could collide at the host when their launch-drawn phases align. Per-window cross-card “data ready” first-arrival spread and ≤5µs collision fraction, stalled vs quick, per draw (card_phase.py). REFUTED Signs are opposite to the prediction: stalled windows have ~2× LARGER arrival spread (a symptom of the stall), and tighter packing correlates with FASTER draws (+0.47). Card streams colliding at µs granularity is not the stall trigger.
H8 · dose-response: is host-memory contention CAUSAL?tp2 is known-tight; the antagonist injects controlled DRAM read pressure from four non-tron cores (~80 GB/s vs the workload’s own ~19.5). If memory-path contention causes the lottery, tp2 must start rolling under the dose; if tp2 stays tight, bulk-bandwidth contention is excluded and the card side is what remains. A/B on 3c51: 12 draws tp2 bare, then 12 draws tp2 + 4× membw (each core streams ~20 GB/s of reads through a 512 MB buffer). EXCLUDED (cause AND amplifier) Three campaigns, 36 draws total. tp2 bare: TIGHT (130.665–131.861, CV 0.32%). tp2 + 80 GB/s dose: still tight (CV 0.36%, mean unchanged) and ZERO stalled fills in any tp2 draw — the stall phenomenon does not exist below 4 cards. tp4 + the same dose (campaign dir misnamed 3c51-tp2antag-20260812T191334Z, contents are tp4): lottery unchanged (CV 1.14% vs baseline 1.13%, gap 3.92% vs 3.75%, fill-stall rates 0.5–1.3% vs 0.5–3.9%), mean cost only −2.5%. Host memory pressure neither creates nor modulates the lottery.

H3 result (computed this step, on the 20 pfgate draws): stalls arrive memorylessly

For each draw, a window counts as stalled if its span exceeds 1500µs (the two-population split from the pfgate report). Across all 20 draws the distances between consecutive stalled windows behave like independent coin flips:

  • CV of inter-arrival distances: median 1.00 (range 0.88–1.22). A value near 1 is the signature of a memoryless (Poisson) process; a periodic interferer gives ≪1, bursts give ≫1.
  • Lag-1 autocorrelation of the stall indicator: median 0.017 (essentially zero — a stalled window does not make the next window more likely to stall).
  • Runs test z-score: median −1.05; only 3 of 20 draws below −2 (mild clustering at most).

Reading: no periodic external activity, no interference episodes. Each window trips the transient independently with a probability that is set at launch (5.7% in the fastest draw → 34.6% in the slowest). A launch-dependent probability of a per-window sleep/wake event is exactly the H2 shape; a firmware poller (H1) would tend to be periodic. Analyzer: stall_arrival.py (CV, autocorrelation, runs test per draw).

5 · Addendum — 2026-08-13 findings

5.1 · The lottery variable on this host: per-block delivery cadence

Decoding the per-block consume stamps (tag 7500+ix; tile assignment recovered exactly for 4096/4096 fills in all 16 smicount draws, percard_arrival.py): the four tiles’ arrivals form a stable staircase (~230/295/380/465µs last-arrival; tile 3 laggard in 82% of fills), and in slow draws the staircase amplifies down the chain while tile 0 stays constant. Splitting inter-stamp gaps: consume work is only 62–75µs/fill; the rest is ~75 arrival waits whose median grows 2.9→3.7µs (+28%) from the fastest to the slowest draw — the whole 118-block train trickles uniformly slower. At ~2.6 KB per block per 3.5µs (~0.74 GB/s/tile) the pace is card compute/stream-out cadence, not link capacity. Labeled hypothesis for the FPGA team: wcls is the most HBM-bandwidth-bound matmul on the card; a per-launch effective-HBM-bandwidth state (e.g. temperature-dependent refresh) would modulate exactly this cadence while leaving the 3.6M small matmuls flat and being placement-independent (v9 hash).

5.2 · Freeze hygiene: the deep outliers are a separate phenomenon

A full audit (20 campaigns, 256 draws, both hosts) found 26 draws polluted by ~0.19 s freezes (mode 0.14–0.22 s plus 2–3× multiples) whose summed duration explains each deep outlier’s deficit exactly (e.g. 148.44→186.7 tok/s after subtraction). They strike at arbitrary pipeline points, cluster in wall-clock episodes, and are environmental (SMI/NMI/cgroup/kernel-log all clean; not reproduced by deliberate load). Standing rule: draws with >50 ms inter-record holes are excluded from lottery statistics. One conclusion retracted by the clean re-audit: msrsamp’s wide CV was entirely freeze-driven (2.15→1.02%), so no jitter is attributed to the 150µs sampler.

5.3 · Host-clock root cause (cross-host texture caveat)

The 2.70 vs ~4.1 GHz busy-clock difference between this host and 3bda is SST-CP class-of-service assignment: the harness’s CLOS setup silently no-ops here (missing intel-speed-select binary + || true), leaving all tron cores in CLOS3, capped at 2700 MHz — tracked as tron issue #3751 (tooling robustness; machine state deliberately unchanged). Within-campaign A/Bs on this page are unaffected (state constant); cross-host texture comparisons (fat-mode here vs stall-rate on 3bda) are confounded by it. Also excluded along the way: the IOMMU/DMAR path (all VT-d counters flat or zero across the lottery, 20 ungated draws).

5.4 · Definitive sync points and the fence-bracketed measurement

The decode token cycle has exactly two definitive sync points (glossary): FENCE 1 (workers_done → 0; source-verified: launch_wcls runs strictly after the join, so hardware is empty there) and FENCE 3 (listeners_notified return). The no-definitive-point gap [F1→F3] is exactly the streaming region — concurrent by design. A dedicated session (trace-sync-points) is instrumenting both. First results (tag 7600, campaign 3c51-fence3-tp4-20260813T050910Z, 16/16, hash unchanged): the C.rest split lands entirely on the construction side — cb→F3 flat (corr +0.11; scheduler wake at the definitive sync point excluded), F3→endpoint 410k→521k cycles, corr −0.79; the FENCE-3-to-FENCE-3 period reconciles with TPS to 0.01%. The tag-7601 (FENCE 1) campaign (3c51-fence13-tp4-20260813T060034Z, 16/16, hash unchanged) then delivered a zero-residual fence attribution: span growth +294k cycles = open→F1 +176k (corr −0.65: the 70-worker join convoy MOVES with the lottery — codex F1 is a first-class carrier) + F1→wcls-dispatch +23k (corr −0.81) + wcls-dispatch→F3 +71k + F3→end +24k. Caveat: two campaigns 50 min apart expressed the lottery through different legs (fill-dominated vs join-convoy-dominated) — the manifestation moves between waiting legs; the shared cause is upstream of all of them. Full treatment: stall-map §3.5; their report: trace-sync-points/status_report/2026-08-13-01-fence3-split.html.

The streamed-logits mechanism (what fill waits ON)

NaN-sentinel block latch
tron h/libpos.hpp:203-223

struct stream_result_t {
  static constexpr uint16_t nans = 0xffff;
  ...
  void prepare() noexcept {
    // Set the last 8 bytes of each result block to nans.
    for (size_t block_ix = 0; block_ix < blocks; ++block_ix) {
      bf16* block_end = begin + std::min<size_t>(result_size, (block_ix + 1) * res_elts_per_block);
      uint16_t* latch = reinterpret_cast<uint16_t*>(block_end) - 1;
      *latch = nans;
    }
  }

Before launch, the host writes 0xffff into the tail of every result block; a block has ARRIVED when the card DMA overwrites that latch. This stream bypasses the normal rx completion ring.

Glossary

  • inter-fwd-pass (window) — the once-per-token span from the last layer’s attention barrier through the lm-head matmul, the streamed logits arrival, token pick, and the next step’s first dispatch.
  • corr — Pearson correlation coefficient between a per-draw quantity and that draw’s decode TPS; −1 = grows exactly when the launch is slower, 0 = unrelated.
  • fast4 / slow4 — means over the 4 fastest / 4 slowest draws of a campaign.
  • SMI — System Management Interrupt: the firmware suspends all CPU cores and runs its own code; the OS cannot see the pause except as lost time. MSR 0x34 counts them per core.
  • C-state — hardware CPU sleep level; deeper states save power but cost wake-up time and cache warmth. /dev/cpu_dma_latency is the kernel interface that bounds how deep cores may sleep.
  • wcls / lm-head — the final matrix multiply that turns the hidden state into logits (word scores); its result streams back to the host in 118 blocks.
  • fill_logits_buffer — host function that waits for and consumes those streamed blocks (defined model.hpp:3184; timed via the tag-7000 stamp at its call site :3159–3163).
  • HBM — the card’s on-package memory where weights live; “placement” = which addresses each weight tensor gets at load time.
  • definitive sync point — project term (2026-08-13): an instant that every operation on every thread is definitively before or after — nothing concurrent with it (CS: quiescent point / inevitable global state / BSP barrier). The token cycle has TWO: FENCE 1 (workers_done → 0 inside plugin_state.run() — hardware empty, wcls launches only afterwards; source-verified 2026-08-13) and FENCE 3 (listeners_notified return, model.hpp:3082–3083). Neither span edge is one. FENCE 3 is the canonical phase-1/phase-2 cut inside the window; [F1→F3] is the irreducible streaming region with no definitive point inside.
  • draw — one full launch of runtron (load + benchmark); the lottery is drawn per launch.
